title: MySQL Examples
description: Copy-ready MySQL snippets for everyday tasks: creating a schema, bulk inserts and upserts, pagination, reports with joins and GROUP BY, indexes, accounts, transactions, JSON and backups. Run them in your own MySQL 8.4 or 9 client.

examples.title: Create a database and tables
examples.description: A database with explicit utf8mb4 settings and two InnoDB tables linked by a named foreign key, with auto-increment keys, defaults and an ENUM status.

examples.title: Upsert with ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
examples.description: Insert a row or, when the unique email already exists, update the city instead. Uses the row alias syntax from MySQL 8.0.20.

examples.title: Page through rows with keyset pagination
examples.description: Offset pagination for the first pages and keyset pagination for deep pages, which stays fast because it seeks the index instead of skipping rows.

examples.title: Customers with order counts and revenue
examples.description: A LEFT JOIN report that keeps customers without orders, counting with COUNT(o.id) and turning the NULL sum into 0.00 with COALESCE.
examples.code:
SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS orders,
       COALESCE(SUM(k.price * o.quantity), 0) AS revenue
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN coffees k ON k.id = o.coffee_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY revenue DESC;

examples.title: Revenue per month
examples.description: Group orders by calendar month with DATE_FORMAT and sum the line totals; output for the rows loaded in the CRUD lesson.
examples.code:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(o.ordered_at, '%Y-%m') AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       SUM(k.price * o.quantity) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN coffees k ON k.id = o.coffee_id
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

examples.title: Comma-separated list per group
examples.description: GROUP_CONCAT with ORDER BY and SEPARATOR builds one sorted list of coffees for each customer who has ordered.
examples.code:
SELECT c.name,
       GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT k.name ORDER BY k.name SEPARATOR ', ') AS coffees
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN coffees k ON k.id = o.coffee_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;

examples.title: Add a composite index and check the plan
examples.description: Create an index on the columns a query filters by, then confirm with EXPLAIN that the access type changed from ALL to ref.
examples.code:
CREATE INDEX idx_coffees_origin_roast ON coffees (origin, roast);

EXPLAIN SELECT name FROM coffees WHERE origin = 'Brazil' AND roast = 'dark';

examples.title: Read-only reporting role and account
examples.description: Bundle SELECT on a database into a role, grant it to a reporting account restricted to one network, and make it active on login.

examples.title: Sell stock inside a transaction
examples.description: Lock the stock row with FOR UPDATE, decrement it and insert the order, committing both changes together so concurrent sales cannot oversell.

examples.title: Back up and restore with mysqldump
examples.description: A consistent logical backup of one database including stored programs, restored into a separate database for verification.
examples.code:
# Back up
mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --events \
  -u root -p roastery > roastery-$(date +%F).sql

# Restore into a fresh database and check it
mysql -u root -p -e "CREATE DATABASE roastery_restore"
mysql -u root -p roastery_restore < roastery-2026-11-14.sql
mysql -u root -p -e "SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders FROM roastery_restore.orders"
